liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Jack Straw** (2 reviews): Opener had already been played in Boston two shows (three nights) earlier, disappointing a fan arriving on the floor; Garcia's solos are sweet and lyrical [8][16]
- **In The Midnight Hour** (2 reviews): The Midnight Hour into Cumberland Blues sequence is singled out as hot; The posted track list is wrong; Midnight Hour into Cumberland actually opens the second set [11][15]
- **Uncle John's Band** (2 reviews): The jam coming out of it is described as interesting; Garcia's middle solo is less focused, but the coda has him working out a melody on low strings [9][17]
- **Deal** (1 review): Runs about 13 minutes, roughly double typical jamming versions, steadily building in intensity [9]
- **Cumberland Blues** (1 review): Played at a galloping pace within the second set [9]
- **Playing In The Band** (1 other source): Leads into Uncle John's Band and an extended jam that passes through various partial-band combinations and the drummers [4]
- **Drums (2)** (1 review): Garcia took part in a nice jam stretching through the drums segment [14]
- **Standing On The Moon** (1 review): Described as an especially beautiful version [16]

## Setlist highlights

- **In The Midnight Hour**: back after 119 archived shows (549 days) [19]

## The recordings

- **gd1994-10-05.aud.bleich.sirmick.79258.flac16** (recommended): audience recording; 19 songs; 156 min; rated 2.5/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd94-10-05.sbd.unknown.8030.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 18 songs; 152 min; rated 4.71/5 by 31 [5]. Said about its sound: Garcia's singing comes across good, not hoarse or strained, and his guitar is focused [17]
- **gd1994-10-05.151083.dsbd.miller.flac1644**: soundboard; 18 songs; 163 min; rated 3.5/5 by 4 [2]
- **gd1994-10-05.schoeps.wklitz-jones.85225.flac1648**: source not stated; 18 songs; 168 min; rated 4/5 by 3 [3]

## Around the show

- Garcia remained on stage throughout drums and afterward [8]
- Reviewer was stuck in traffic and missed the first set [11]
- Reviewer ranks it among the year's best, topped only by the 8/1/94 show [7]
- Jerry's stamina had been criticized at Seattle and Eugene shows weeks earlier; this show countered that [8]
- Judged the best of the three nights at the Spectrum that fall [12]
- Reviewer considers it the highlight of the fall 1994 Spectrum run [14]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1994-10-05.aud.bleich.sirmick.79258.flac16**: taped by John Bleich (taper section row 1  seat 19  Section 107); transferred by SirMick; source: aud > WMD-6 with Nak 300 shotguns > mac > wav > flac [1]. Also: Audience recording by Bleich; slight noise reduction applied to the latter half of disc 2, around Quinn [1]
- **gd94-10-05.sbd.unknown.8030.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD > DAT > CDR [5]
- **gd1994-10-05.151083.dsbd.miller.flac1644**: transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  December 7, 2020; source: SBD > DAT Master (Panasonic SV-3700/44.1k) > DAT (Panasonic SV-3800) [2]
- **gd1994-10-05.schoeps.wklitz-jones.85225.flac1648**: taped by Keith Litzenberger & Roger Jones; source: Schoeps MK4's>Reutelhuber>Sony TCD-D10PROII [3]
